CharacterFiles.index_meaning: [roster slot 0..53][track 0..18]. Roster slot order: Mario, Luigi, DK, Diddy, Peach, Daisy, Yoshi, Baby Mario, Baby Luigi, Bowser, Wario, Waluigi, Koopa(red), Toad(red), Boo, Toadette, Shy Guy(red), Birdo, Monty, Bowser Jr, Paratroopa(red), Pianta x3, Noki x3, Hammer Bro, Toadsworth, Toad x4, Magikoopa x4, King Boo, Petey, Dixie, Goomba, Paragoomba, Koopa(green), Paratroopa(green), Shy Guy x4, Dry Bones x4, Fire Bro, Boomerang Bro (not character id; id->slot goes through the table at 0x80108DB8). Track 0 = full-detail model pack (gpc+tpl), track 1 = low-detail model pack for distant cameras, tracks 2..18 = 17 animation banks. Track 8 is frequently the same-size shared bank (210656 bytes) and track 14 is a 15742-byte bank common to almost all slots. Variant slots reuse the base slot's anim entries (same entry ids) but have unique model entries.
CharacterFiles.evidence: fn_80021BBC (0x80021BBC, build/GYQE01/asm/auto_fn_80021BBC_text.s @80021C60-80021C84): `mulli r5, r30, 0x13` then adds lbl_800F1D78 and ARAMTransfers 19 descriptors (the preceding block does the same kind of copy from lbl_800EFD38) - i.e. row = roster slot, 19 descriptors per row. A pointer to the table is also kept in sdata lbl_803CB790 (.4byte lbl_800F1D78), read by animationInitializat*, fn_80014A18, fn_80014D4C, fn_80014E50, fn_80014F40, fn_80015468 (animation/model loaders). Content: 1026 contiguous descriptors = 54 x 19, no gaps, size 0x4020 exact; each row starts with two 'character model' containers (mario00.gpc, luigi00.gpc, ... HB00.gpc) followed by 17 anim banks. Colour-variant rows (Pianta, Noki, Toad, Magikoopa, Shy Guy, Dry Bones, Bros) have their own model entries but repeat the base slot's anim entry ids. Matches E:/Project Rio/MSSB Editor/zzzzdat/chars.py ('Sub-files table at 0x800F1D78: 54 slots x 19 tracks', TRACKS = 19, SLOT_NAMES).
CharacterFiles.review: Confirmed in build/GYQE01/asm/auto_fn_80021BBC_text.s at 80021C60: mulli r5,r30,0x13 then the base lbl_800F1D78, so 19 descriptors per row. Size 0x4020 = 54*19*16 matches symbols.txt. The name follows the sibling StadiumFiles at 0x800EFBE8. grep -w finds no CharacterFiles in config, src or include. The index is the roster slot, not the character id; put that in a comment. Not checked: the evidence file, zzzzdat/chars.py, the lbl_803CB790 pointer and its reader functions, so the 54-slot order and track meanings are unverified. The 54x19 shape rests on the asm stride and the 0x4020 size.

AramCharacterFiles.index_meaning: Four consecutive runs, lengths in lbl_803CB7E0: [0..53] by character slot id (54 slots; 0-32 model containers, 33-53 variant texture sets); [54..431] = 54 + charSlot*7 + item (item 0 L hand, 1 R hand, 2 L glove, 3 R glove, 4 batting, 5 pitching, 6 catching hand-pose track); [432..485] by character slot -> animation file (variants repeat the base entry id); [486..514] hand-pose event set id 0..28.
AramCharacterFiles.evidence: fn_800227E4 (ARAM preload init, allocs 0x4D6600) walks the table in consecutive runs whose lengths come from sdata lbl_803CB7E0 = {0x36, 0x17A, 0x36, 0x1D} (54+378+54+29 = 515 = size 0x2030/16) and stores each file's ARAM address into pointer arrays at lbl_803716B8+0x1D8/0x1DC/0x1E0/0x1E4. fn_8002254C queues ARAMTransfer of slot [idx] (run 0, addr array +0x1D8); fn_8002244C queues slot [0x36 + (slot<<0 | sub) ] using addr array +0x1DC (arg = charSlot<<16 | flat index); fn_80021ADC/fn_80021BBC (index < 0x1D) read slot [0x1E6 + i] via ARAMTransfer mode 3 when the ARAM-preloaded flag (0x1EA bit 3) is set, else fall back to lbl_800F71D8[i]. Contents: slots 0-32 character model containers (mario00.gpc ... HB00.gpc), 33-53 texture sets for the colour-variant character slots; 54-431 seven files per character slot (L_hand, R_hand, L_glove, R_glove, 3 hand-pose tracks); 432-485 one animation file per character slot; 486-514 the 29 shared hand-pose event sets. Editor zzzzdat/chars.py calls this the 'master' table with the same layout.
AramCharacterFiles.review: The build asm shows fn_800227E4, the function at 0x8002244C, fn_80021ADC and fn_80021BBC all referencing lbl_800EFD38, and fn_80021ADC falls back to lbl_800F71D8. lbl_803CB7E0 is 8 bytes of 2-byte data, which fits the four run lengths claimed. The editor's chars.py agrees on the layout. I did not re-derive the 0x36 and 0x1E6 offsets instruction by instruction. 'chara' is used in the decomp's symbol names, the 'Table' suffix matches audioFileTable and relFileTable, and nothing collides.

CharacterHandFiles.index_meaning: [character slot id 0..53][0 L hand (batting), 1 R hand (batting), 2 L glove, 3 R glove, 4 L hand (pitching), 5 R hand (pitching)]
CharacterHandFiles.evidence: Only reached through the sdata pointer lbl_803CB7A8 (-> lbl_800F5D98), read by fn_80014204, fn_800145F8, fn_80019C00, fn_8001A3FC. fn_80014204 loops 0x36 (54) character slots alongside the s16 table lbl_800EEAAC and takes the max flags_size of descriptor [i] to size a buffer. 324 slots = 54 * 6, contents strictly periodic: L_hand07, R_hand07, L_glove01, R_glove01, L_hand07, R_hand07; variant slots repeat the base character's entry ids. Editor chars.py HAND_TABLE_VA/HAND_TABLE_ROLES: first hand pair = batting, second = pitching (they differ only in the hand-pose event track section). These are the non-ARAM (disc) copies, entry ids 1505-1702.
CharacterHandFiles.review: The facts hold: sdata lbl_803CB7A8 holds a pointer to lbl_800F5D98 (sdata asm line 75), and fn_80014204 and fn_800145F8 load through it. The symbol size 0x1440 is 54 slots times 6 descriptors, and chars.py HAND_TABLE_VA and HAND_TABLE_ROLES match the claimed index meaning. The sibling descriptor tables are named *FileTable (audioFileTable, relFileTable, the proposed aramCharaFileTable), so I renamed it for consistency. charaHandFileTable does not collide with anything.

HandPoseEventSetFiles.review: fn_80021ADC loads lbl_800EFD38 on one path and lbl_800F71D8 on the other, so the fallback claim stands. sdata lbl_803CB794 points at lbl_800F71D8, and the dossier shows 30 descriptors ending at +0x1D0 inside a 0x2A0 symbol. chars.py EVENT_COPY_VA calls it the copy of the hand-pose event sets outside the ARAM chunk. I added the *FileTable suffix to match the sibling tables; the new name does not collide. Slot 29 and the trailing 0xC0 bytes are still unexplained, so treat the split at +0x1E0 as pending.
